string.text: The fertile valley of the Great River Anduin, home to the Beornings and Woodmen. Simple folk who live between the Misty Mountains and Mirkwood.
The coastal realm of Bellakar, settled by Numenorean Faithful who remained true to the Valar. A bastion of civilization on the southern shores.
50% less forest speed penalty + 15% sight range (Battanian-borrowed)
+20% chance for veteran militia in towns (Battanian-borrowed)

The Hill-Men of Dunland, ancient enemies of the Rohirrim. Battanian forest traditions blend with TAOM's Hill Marchers and Hill-Tribe Levies — cheap, fast, angry warbands that march on plain and forest alike. Battanian smiths are slow, but warbands are not.
+10% party speed on plains and +5% party size — Dunlending warbands cover ground fast.
+10% village volunteer respawn rate — villages refill with cousins fast.
Borrowed 50% less forest speed penalty + 15% sight, and +20% chance for veteran militia in towns; -10% construction speed.
Scattered Orc tribes in the frozen northern wastes near the Ice Bay of Forochel. Savage raiders who prey on the Lossoth and any who venture north.
-15% mounted recruit and upgrade cost (War Wargs)
+10% party speed on plains and swamps (Forced March, Fenland Drillmasters)
+2 Merchant + 1 Artisan + 12 Gang Leader notables in Isengard town (20 total)

Saruman's industrial fortress at Orthanc. The Ring of Isengard runs day and night — Uruk-hai legions, forge-line crossbows, war wargs. Isengard's one town swells to twenty notables: a recruitment hub equal to many cities of Rohan. Saruman's Grip alienates every neighbor.
+20% party size limit and +10% march speed on plain and swamp.
+15% construction, -20% smithing energy, -15% mounted recruitment cost.
Isengard's single town swells to 20 notables — 4 Merchant, 2 Artisan, 14 Gang Leader.
Both speed and weight in melee
Heavy crossbow line from the forge-pits.
Fast hit-and-run cavalry of the White Hand.
-60% army influence cost (The Dark Lord's Will)
+10% party speed at night (Creatures of the Dark)
+5% party speed on plains and swamps (Shadow March, Dead Marshes)
+2 Gang Leader notables per town (Black Speech Heralds)

Sauron's Black Land. The Dark Lord's Will lets armies muster at minimal influence cost; Nurn Farmlands feed the hordes; Sauron's Wrath turns raids into slaughter; Creatures of the Dark march faster at night than any free people in daylight. Dark Tribute drains the treasury.
Army influence cost reduced by 60% — Sauron's hordes need no consensus.
+25% raid damage and +5% party speed on plains and swamps.
+10% party speed at night — the eyes of Mordor never sleep.
Almost no influence required to march

A distinct goblin host of the Blue Mountains (Ered Luin) in the far west, hard by the Grey Havens of Lindon — a realm apart from their Misty Mountains cousins of Goblin Town. Same numberless, ill-armed swarms: weak alone, overwhelming in the mass, and ravenous on the march. They trouble the Elves of the western shore.
+40% party size and +25% village volunteer respawn — weak but numberless.
+10% party speed on snow — goblins know every crag and tunnel.
The horde devours everything — +20% party food consumption.
Numberless bow-armed rabble of the high crags.

The teeming goblin-warrens beneath the High Pass of the Misty Mountains. Since the fall of the Great Goblin the tribes have multiplied without number — vast, ill-armed swarms that win by sheer weight and breed faster than any foe can cull them. They run swiftest over the snows of their mountain home, but such hordes are ever ravenous.
+40% party size and +25% village volunteer respawn — goblins are weak but numberless.
+10% party speed on snow — goblins know every pass and tunnel of the Misty Mountains.
Such a horde devours everything — +20% party food consumption.
Massed spear-fodder of the High Pass warrens.
Numberless bow-armed rabble of the tunnels.
Heavier shock-goblin of the deep warrens.
-10% mounted recruit and upgrade cost (Khuzait, inherited)
+25% horse, mule, cow, and sheep village production (Khuzait, inherited)

The Easterlings of the eastern plains. Inherited Khuzait cavalry traditions paired with TAOM's Easterling Outriders steppe speed and Easterling Host party size. Heavy cavalry that arrives in numbers and tribute.
+10% party speed on steppe — riders of the Sea of Rhun cross the plain fast.
+5% party size limit — hordes muster in answer to Mordor's call.
Inherited Khuzait -10% mounted cost, +25% animal village production; -20% town tax income.

The corsair haven and Black Numenorean port-city on the southern bays. Corsair Trade slashes caravan costs, Corsair Glory adds renown, Desert Corsairs march fast across the sands — but Corsair Greed inflates every wage bill.
-25% caravan cost and +15% tariff income — Umbar prospers on every passing ship.
+8% renown per battle — the corsair name is sung in every port.
+10% party speed on desert — Umbar's marches cross sand as easily as sea.
+20% village hearth growth (The Last Homely House)

The green land west of the Blue Mountains, last realm of the High Elves on the shores of Middle-earth. From the Grey Havens of Mithlond the white ships sail into the West. Círdan the Shipwright, eldest of the Eldar, keeps the fading light of the Noldor — wise, few, and each blade irreplaceable. Lindon shares the Noldor strength of Imladris.
+35% influence awarded on army success — the Wise know how to lead.
+20% village hearth growth and -15% party food consumption.
+10% party speed in forest and +0.5 settlement loyalty per day.
Wise leadership reaps greater influence from victory
Legendary first-age veteran of the Eldar.
Heavy Noldor guardian of the Grey Havens.
50% less forest speed penalty + 15% sight range (Battanian, inherited)
+20% chance for veteran militia in towns (Battanian, inherited)
The Variag of Khand. Battanian forest militia traditions inherited; TAOM's Steppe Charioteers add +10% party speed on steppe on top. Mercenary bands ride for whoever pays the most coin.
+10% party speed on steppe — Variag chariots roll fast.
Mercenary captains ride for whoever pays — but they keep their cut.
Inherited 50% less forest speed penalty + 15% sight range and +20% chance for veteran militia in towns; -10% construction speed.
Mercenary captains are loyal to coin, not lord
The last and greatest of the successor kingdoms of Arnor. Arthedain held out longest against the Witch-king of Angmar before its final fall.
The successor realm of Cardolan, once part of the great kingdom of Arnor. Now a land of scattered settlements and ancient barrows haunted by wights.
+20% relationship penalty from kingdom decisions (Sturgian, inherited)
-0.5 settlement loyalty per day (Small Territory Exposure)

Bard's rebuilt city beneath Erebor. Inherited Sturgian grain abundance and Sturgian cheap-army tradition pair with TAOM's Vale Traders plain-speed bonus — but Sturgian kingdom-decision penalties cut both ways. A thriving trade alliance with the Dwarves keeps Dale rich and ready.
+10% party speed on plains — caravans of Lake-town move fast.
Trade with Erebor provides bonus income and arms-supply.
Inherited Sturgian +10% village grain and -50% army influence cost; relationship penalty +20% on kingdom decisions.
The wine-growing realm of Dorwinion on the northwestern shores of the Sea of Rhun. A prosperous trading kingdom caught between the Free Peoples and the East.

The Lonely Mountain reclaimed. Master Smiths cut smithing energy by 30%; Dwarven Honor adds loyalty every day; Dwarven Stubbornness keeps morale unshakable. Slow to build a wall — but the wall holds until the mountain itself falls.
-30% smithing energy cost — Dwarven forges work twice as fast.
-25% garrison wage and +1 settlement loyalty per day.
+5 party morale and +10% village production — Dwarves do not bend.
The Dwarven mansions of the Blue Mountains, ancestral halls of Durin's Folk. After the loss of Erebor, many Dwarves found refuge here before Thorin's quest.
+20% village hearth growth (The Last Homely House)

Elrond's hidden valley, sanctuary of the Wise. Elven Wisdom unifies armies at little influence cost; the Last Homely House grows hearths in every village. Elven Pride still drives every council — every Noldor blade is irreplaceable.
+35% influence awarded on army success — the Wise know how to lead.
+20% village hearth growth and -15% party food consumption.
+10% party speed in forest — the trees of Imladris part for their kin.

Thranduil's Woodland Realm in northern Mirkwood. Silvan archers and veteran militia hold the great forest against spider, orc, and shadow. Woodland Sustenance keeps the supplies light; Woodland Bonds keep morale high. Forest isolation slows growth.
+10% party speed in forest and -15% food consumption.
+25% chance militia recruits arrive as veterans.
+3 party morale — Silvan elves march with songs.

The Golden Wood, realm of Lady Galadriel and Lord Celeborn. Wardens of Lorien defend the mallorn-forests cheaply; Lembas Bread sustains every march; Elven Harmony keeps morale unshakable. Timeless Craft means every change is slow.
+10% party speed in forest and -20% garrison wage.
-15% party food consumption — one bite carries a marching elf a day.
+3 party morale and +0.5 loyalty per day in every settlement.
Heavy Elven guardian of the Golden Wood.

The orc-host that holds the deep places of the Misty Mountains — the black pits of Moria, won from the Dwarves, and the cold peaks from Caradhras to Methedras. Larger and better-armed than the goblin rabble of the High Pass, they muster vast war-hosts for almost no influence and march hungry but tireless across the snows.
Army recruitment costs 40% less influence — the orc-host needs no consensus to march.
+30% party size and +10% speed on snow — large war-hosts bred to the cold peaks.
A war-host of this size eats greedily — +15% party food consumption.
Almost no influence to muster armies
Hold the deep places of Moria
Heavier orc infantry of the deep halls.
Bow-orc of the deep halls and high tunnels.
Raider bred in the dark of Khazad-dûm.
Weaker troops than Men or Elves
Universally hated by the Free Peoples
An Elven realm in the northern reaches of Mirkwood, where the Wood-elves maintain their ancient forests against the creeping darkness from the south.
The wild hill country of Rhudaur, easternmost of Arnor's successor kingdoms. Fell under the influence of Angmar and its hill-men serve the Witch-king.
-15% mounted troop wages (Riders of the Mark)
+10% party speed on plains (Riders of the Plains)
-10% party speed when over 50% infantry (Cavalry Dependent)

The Riddermark of the Horse-lords. Horse-lord Heritage cheapens every mounted recruit and upgrade; Riders of the Mark cuts mounted wages; Horse-lord Fellowship binds the Mark in loyalty. Cavalry Dependent — parties heavy with infantry slow to a crawl.
-15% cost to recruit AND upgrade mounted troops — the Mark trains riders cheaply.
-15% mounted troop wages and +10% party speed on plains.
+5 party morale and +0.5 settlement loyalty per day.
Elite heavy cavalry of the King.
Cavalry Dependent — infantry-heavy parties slow down
Helm's Deep is exposed when the Mark rides out
+1 Merchant + 1 Artisan + 13 Gang Leader notables in Dol Guldur town (20 total)

The Necromancer's southern hold in Mirkwood. Shadow Command rallies hordes at almost no influence; Dark Conscription drills militia veterans; Shadow Captains swell the one town to twenty notables. Voracious Hordes eat as much as they slay.
Army influence cost reduced by 50% — dread compels obedience.
+20% party size and +20% volunteer respawn rate.
Dol Guldur's single town fields 20 notables — a 15 Gang Leader recruitment hub.
+1 Artisan + 3 Gang Leader notables per town (Bone-Smiths, Pale Warband Chieftains)

Mount Gundabad, sacred to the Pale Orcs of Bolg's lineage. Vast warbands march from the high passes — Orc Horde discipline rallies hosts for almost no influence, Mountain Marauders rule the snows, and Plunder Demands keep every warlord paid.
Army influence cost reduced by 40% — dread compels obedience.
+20% party size limit and +10% party speed on snow.
+3 Gang Leader and +1 Artisan notable per town — recruitment swells with raiders.
Raid economy keeps the larder full
Dwarves and Elves hate the Pale Orcs
The dread realm of the Witch-king of Angmar in the far north. From his fortress of Carn Dum, the Witch-king wages war upon the remnants of Arnor.
+10% party speed on plains (Men of the Fields)
+1 settlement loyalty per day (Tower Guard Discipline)

The last bastion of the Dunedain in the south. Tower Guard hold the line, Gondorian Discipline rallies armies cheaply, and the Men of the Fields march on plains. War-Depleted Lands grow slowly — but Gondor stands.
-20% garrison wage and +1 settlement loyalty per day.
+5 party morale and +30% army influence awarded on success.
+10% party speed on plains and +2.5% party size — the Pelennor is open ground.
Elite armored infantry of Minas Tirith.
Elite units bound to specific regions
A region dominated by savage Orc tribes from the eastern mountains. Fierce raiders who terrorize the borderlands between Khand and Harad.
A desolate eastern region overrun by Orc tribes. These savage bands raid the borderlands and serve as scouts for the forces of darkness.
+10% party speed on desert (Sons of the Sun)
-30% caravan build cost + -10% trade penalty (Aserai Trader, inherited)
No speed penalty on desert (Aserai Desert, inherited)

The Haradrim of Harwan, sons of the sun. Aserai desert resilience inherited; TAOM's Sons of the Sun add +10% party speed on desert; Haradrim Warbands add party size on top of the inherited caravan economy. Mumakil rule the southern plains.
+10% party speed on desert — born to burning sands.
+5% party size limit — tribal warbands ride together to Mordor's call.
Inherited Aserai Trader (-30% caravans, -10% trade penalty) and Aserai Desert (no desert speed penalty); +5% daily wages.
Long-bow elite of the deep south.
The wild lands of Enedwaith between Arnor and Gondor. Home to scattered clans of Men who answer to no king, living as hunters and herders.
